P-D1.1.text: (leakage exists at all.) In every A2-successful cell, the share of the 11,000 benign items whose absolute shift exceeds the clean arm's maximum seed-to-seed absolute shift is greater than 0. If this FAILS, no benign-reference defence - stratified, sliced or otherwise - can detect this attack, and that is the defence's answer.
P-D1.1.caveat: choice (w): the reference is a per-seed MAXIMUM over 33,000 seed-to-seed differences, so a FAIL would not by itself show that aggregate detection is impossible; leak_share is over items x seeds

P-D1.2.text: (anchor; must hold or the inputs are wrong.) The global 4c Gaussian ratio recomputed here stays inside (0.5, 2.0) in all 3 A2-successful cells, and the global check's firing count over the 30 cells is exactly 7, reproducing D-440 (3)'s P-A2.2 count.

P-D1.3.text: (slicing helps, primary.) At the matched clean-arm false-alarm rate, the per-slice check fires in strictly more than 7 of the 30 cells.
P-D1.3.reason: the statistic is undefined below the top fifth (the author, D-443 (1); prereg section 11.3; P-D1.5 withdrawn for the same reason by D-181)

P-D1.4.text: (slicing helps where it matters.) At that same matched rate, it fires in at least 2 of the 3 A2-successful cells. Registered with its weakness stated: with 3 cells this is low-powered, and a FAIL is informative only together with P-D1.3.
P-D1.4.reason: the statistic is undefined below the top fifth (the author, D-443 (1); prereg section 11.3; P-D1.5 withdrawn for the same reason by D-181)

P-D1.5.text: (the cost of slicing.) At the matched rate, the per-slice check's false-alarm rate on the clean arm stays within a factor of 1.5 of the global check's, with the D-177 accuracy line (share within x1.5 and median absolute log error, with n) as a standard row.
P-D1.5.reason: the statistic is undefined below the top fifth (the author, D-443 (1); prereg section 11.3; P-D1.5 withdrawn for the same reason by D-181)

A cell whose ratio is not finite and positive IS A MISS (D-322 (4), as src/phase3_a1.py's `accuracy` and src/mlp_probe_d383.py's `accuracy_line` count one): an infinite error, OUTSIDE x1.5 and INSIDE the median, so the registered 80% threshold means what it says. A non-finite cell, and a cell whose realised shift has the OPPOSITE SIGN to c * sigma (a negative ratio), are both misses by this rule. The median is None with median_is_a_miss when it falls on a miss; the same line over the usable cells only is reported beside, never instead

implementation_choices.rule: D-181: the choice nearest D-entry decides; the list is recorded, not cited

choices.a: THE MATCHED CUT IS ONLY EVER WIDENED (section 4.1: 'its per-slice cut is widened until ...'): the candidates are log 2 (the registered cut, |log r| >= log 2 iff r >= 2 or r <= 0.5) and nextafter(v, +inf) for every clean stat v above log 2; tau is the smallest candidate whose clean false-alarm COUNT (stat >= tau over the 3 x 201 clean draws) is at most the global check's clean count. Counts are compared as integers, never as float shares. The record says whether the achieved count EQUALS the global one, is the LARGEST ACHIEVABLE BELOW it, or is already below it at the registered cut (then tau = log 2 and the cut is not narrowed). Section 8 (3) words the candidates without 'above log 2'; 4.1's 'widened' is kept, so tau >= log 2 (no effect: the arm is withdrawn, D-443 (1)).
choices.b: Every false-alarm rate and every 'share of the draws' is over all 201 rows (the frozen split included), as the spec's 603 = 3 x 201 states; the share over the 200 re-partitions alone (rows 1:, D-156's convention) is recorded beside each detection share. 'Fires on the frozen split' is row 0.
choices.c: log r_k is np.log(r_k) when r_k is finite and positive; otherwise (an underflow to 0 or an overflow) it is logsumexp of the per-seed log_gaussian_ratio values minus log J (health's own never-log(0) route) and the count of such slices is recorded; a value that is still not finite counts as |log r_k| = +inf, also counted.
choices.d: The registered sliced version applies healthcheck_d156.crosses to the slice ratios r_k; the number of draws where it disagrees with stat >= log 2 (a last-bit edge) is recorded beside, never used.
choices.e: Slices: np.argsort(pre_cal[:, j], kind="stable") reshaped to K rows of n/K, lowest pre scores first; an n not divisible by K refuses (5000 / 5 = 1000).
choices.f: Leakage: '>' is strict against ref_j; the 99th percentile is np.percentile's default (linear) over items x seeds; the top decile of a seed is its ceil(n/10) highest pre pool scores by stable argsort (1,100 of 11,000).
choices.g: P-D1.2's 'inside (0.5, 2.0)' is read on the frozen-split global ratio (row 0) as NOT crosses(., CUT), the same split A2's success verdict reads (a2_p3 choice (v)).
choices.h: P-D1.5: the overall rates are floored at 1/(3 x 201) and the per-seed rates at 1/201 before the ratio; 'within a factor of 1.5' is |log ratio| <= log 1.5 (a1m_p3.accuracy_line's rule, inclusive).
choices.i: PRIMARY = the cells of the categories that meet D-389 (3)'s overall rule (successful in >= 3 of 5 seeds at c = -2), at c = -2 and successful (category.success.verdict); cross-checked against the verdicts record's a2_overall; anything but exactly 3 cells refuses. BESIDE = every cell whose success verdict is true.
choices.j: Every A2 record and npz this module reads is checked against the two pull manifests and refuses if absent from them or different; the verdicts record's per-cell success and flag and its score-record sha256s must equal the records'. The predictions record of D-440 is not read: no D1 number depends on it.
choices.k: The npz stores the clean seeds 1 and 2 pool / H / pos score matrices and item ids (for the canary arm); clean seed 0's are in every A2 npz and are not duplicated.
choices.l: Category IDs: cat-k by a2_p3.three_largest's order (count descending, ties alphabetical) of the d440 category record's own counts, which must be that record's pick; the record stores each ID's count only.
choices.m: The clean arms are computed once: the pre and clean-seed-0 arrays of the 30 npz are asserted identical bit for bit, and clean seeds 1 and 2 are scored by the one probe set.
choices.n: A3 is bit for bit in `run` (the node, the libraries that wrote the A2 records). `check` takes --max-ulp for a machine whose numpy / scipy differ (the workstation: numpy 2.5.3 / scipy 1.18.1 against the node's 2.2.6 / 1.15.3 gives 1-ULP differences in the Gaussian ratio's last bit); the flags must still be equal, and the count of differing values and the largest ULP distance are printed.
choices.o: Status FINAL only at the registered parameters (30 cells, probe seeds 0-4, 201 draws, K = 5, cut (2.0, 0.5), the 6-thread BLAS pin); otherwise PROVISIONAL. The leakage quantities are DESCRIPTIVE (beyond P-D1.1).
choices.p: D1-ii's matched cut (prereg 11.1 (2)): z has no registered cut, so the candidates are nextafter(v, +inf) for every clean zstat v; tau_z is the smallest candidate whose clean count (zstat >= tau_z over the 3 x 201 clean draws) is at most the global check's clean count G, compared as integers. The record says whether the count EQUALS G or is the LARGEST ACHIEVABLE BELOW it.
choices.q: D1-ii's z_kj is read from the same health() call that gives the Gaussian slice ratio (one call per slice and seed), so the two sliced statistics use the same slices, bit for bit.
choices.r: D1-ii's descriptive cost row (prereg 11.1 (3)): its clean rate over the global check's, floored as choice (h), and the D-177 line over the three clean seeds' per-seed ratios, each rate floored at 1/201.
choices.s: A WITHDRAWN prediction (P-D1.3, P-D1.4, P-D1.5) is written with its text, verdict 'WITHDRAWN BEFORE RUNNING' and the author's reason. No HELD/FAILED is computed for it, and its numbers are not written beside it; the Gaussian sliced counts are in 'detection' and 'clean_false_alarms', labelled withdrawn.
choices.t: A review confound (D-181, descriptive): D1-ii changes the statistic AND adds slicing. So the UNSLICED mean shift (K = 1: health()'s z_mean on the whole calibration part, |z|) is computed beside it, its cut matched to G by the same rule (p) ('meanshift_unsliced_matched'). D1-ii minus it separates slicing from the change of statistic.
choices.u: A review confound (D-181, descriptive): all 30 attacked models sit on clean seed 0, one of the three clean seeds that set tau_z. So the d1_ii block gives clean seed 0's own D1-ii and unsliced rates beside detection, and every cell carries its share of draws minus clean seed 0's, for both versions.
choices.v: Choice (p) and the Gaussian cut refuse when the global count G >= the number of clean comparisons (every count is then achievable, and no smallest candidate exists in the nextafter set).
choices.w: P-D1.1's registered text reads a FAIL as 'no benign-reference defence can detect'. Its arithmetic compares each item and seed with a per-seed MAXIMUM over 33,000 seed-to-seed differences, so a FAIL would not by itself show that aggregate detection is impossible; this caveat is written beside the verdict. leak_share is over items x seeds; the share of items leaking in at least one seed is recorded beside it.

npz.rule: cell|<cat-k>|c=<c>|as<seed>|... per cell; clean<s>|... per clean seed; row 0 of every per-draw array is the frozen split
